errors.text: The central Fe/Co/Ni–Ti antiferromagnetic coupling mechanism is omitted, so the proposed hypothesis does not explain the suppression of saturation magnetization or the altered fcc magnetic ground state.

The response incorrectly implies that the fcc phase exhibits all three transitions; the target assigns the approximately 214 K transition to the C14 phase, while the approximately 1084 K and 168 K transitions arise from the fcc phase.
It does not predict or explain the approximately 667 Oe coercivity at 400 K, instead giving only a noncommittal expectation of increased coercivity.
